newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher as export picture brightens.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher as export picture brightens.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher, led by nearby December, on brighter prospects for U.S. wheat exports, traders said.
"It started yesterday with the cut in ending stocks and world production numbers plus there is talk Egypt will be in for wheat," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co's Chicago-trade house.
Traders said there was talk Egypt would be in the market by the weekend for 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes of wheat.
But the market also took note of news from the European Union which smacked of a potential cutback in subsidies.
An EU agricultural official Wednesday hinted the EU may cut back on export subsidys because of budget problems.
"It's encouraging the EU is slowing down a little," a trader said.
Wheat futures were hit recently by stiff competition for wheat export business including increases in EU subsidies.
Support also came from a shift in government specifications for a parcel of wheat slated for export to Bangladesh.
Wheat closed 1/2 to 9-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up 9-1/4 at $4.00-3/4 a bushel.
